chunks: What al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from al-Ḥasan, from Zurʿah, from Samāʿah, who said:

I asked him about a man who leads the people, and they hear his voice but do not understand what he is saying. He said: If he hears his voice, then that suffices him; and if he does not hear his voice, he should recite for himself. And it has also been narrated that regarding what he does not hear, he has the choice between reciting and not reciting; but the more precautionary view is what we have already stated.

key_terms.صَوْتَهُ: his voice, meaning the audible sound of the Imam's recitation
key_terms.مُخَيَّرٌ: given a choice between two permissible options
key_terms.يَؤُمُّ: leads the people in congregational salat as Imam
key_terms.يَفْقَهُونَ: they understand or comprehend what is being said
key_terms.يُجْزِيهِ: it suffices him and fulfills the requirement

ai.seo_question: What should a person do in congregational salat if he hears the Imam's voice but cannot understand the recitation?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling on recitation behind an Imam in congregational salat when the follower hears the Imam's voice but cannot make out the words. It indicates that merely hearing the Imam's voice is sufficient, while if the voice is not heard, one should recite personally; although another report gives a choice, the more precautionary ruling is to recite when the voice is not heard.
